claims.implementation: backend/arkali/engineering/agent/harness_task.py - the C-22 contract is the primitive `MS §Harness Engineering` names: "The primitive is not 'send a prompt'; the primitive is 'execute a bounded engineering task'." Every engineering task is expressed as a HarnessTask or it is not expressible at all - there is no partially-specified form, because every element is required with no default and extra="forbid" refuses an undeclared attribute. EMPTY IS A BOUND AND ABSENT IS NOT: tools=() declares the task may use no tools, which is a real boundary, while omitting tools declares nothing; that distinction is why no field carries a default, since a default would collapse "explicitly none" and "never stated" into one value. Scalar elements refuse blank strings and repair_budget is a finite non-negative count, so zero repairs is a budget and is not the same as unbounded. The task is frozen, because bounds that can be widened after admission are not bounds. Contract document docs/contracts/harness_task.md.

claims.implementation: backend/arkali/control/policy/agent_authority.py - enforced in CONTROL.POLICY, which the register assigns this requirement to, and NOT in engineering.agent. The reason is structural rather than clerical: a rule about what an agent may not do, enforced inside the agent context, is enforced by the actor it constrains. engineering.agent is layer rank 4 and control.policy is rank 1, so the agent context can call this and can never replace, subclass or shadow it; AgentRole.assert_may_mutate_canonical_requirements and assert_may_accept DELEGATE, and a control asserts the agent context holds neither prohibited_actors nor required_path in its code. BOTH PROHIBITIONS ARE DERIVED, NEVER WRITTEN DOWN: which actors are barred comes from AUTHORITY_MAP.yaml stable_mutation.prohibited_actors, and why self-acceptance is refused comes from stable_mutation.required_path, which lists candidate production and acceptance as SEPARATE stages - a separation this module CHECKS rather than assumes, so a canonical set that merged those stages fails loudly instead of leaving a rule the documents no longer state. Self-acceptance is refused for EVERY actor, not only barred ones, because direct_mutation_permitted_by is empty by design and no actor is exempt from a stage boundary. NO OPERATION CLASS WAS ADDED: unmapped_action_resolution is already DENY, and adding one would change a Protected-Core-owned contract that CONTRACT_INVENTORY.md puts behind HUMAN GATE 2, which this phase has not reached and did not assume. backend/arkali/control/policy/policy_errors.py - ARK-ERR-0095 and ARK-ERR-0096, distinct types so a control can assert WHICH boundary refused.
